_note: EVERY NUMBER HERE IS MEASURED FROM THE MODEL'S VOXELS at the --size the importer was given. None of it is a real-world source; a dimension typed into engine data still needs its own citation (grounding-auditor).
size_basis: NOMINAL - no sourced overall dimension; proportions only. 28 m is inside the strip-building length range of 18-38 m (roman.md 1.4, from m5f_strip_building_grounding.txt); no dimension of the Xanten houses is in the dossier.
eaves_method: top of the highest layer (above 30% of the ridge height) whose silhouette extent across the roof-pitch axis is >= 97% of the widest such layer: the height above which the building only narrows. With an overhanging roof this is the roof's lower edge, not the top of the wall. No pitch axis -> equals the ridge.
eaves_95pct_method: the earlier rule, kept for comparison: top of the highest layer whose solid cross-section is >= 95% of the largest
ridge_method: top of the highest layer whose extent along the ridge axis is >= 50% of the building's (so a chimney or finial is not the ridge)
roof_pitch_method: axis = the horizontal axis along which the silhouette narrows in the top 30% of the height (null if neither does); rise/run = (ridge - eaves) / (half the roof span at the eaves), assumes a symmetric roof; mean gradient = atan of the mean column-top step along that axis between eaves and ridge
storey_method: on each of the two long facades (first surface seen along the shorter plan axis, below the eaves): drop the dominant wall cluster; per remaining cluster drop horizontal runs longer than a quarter of the facade (rail, band course, plinth, roof edge), connected pieces wider than half the facade (frame network) and pieces 3x taller than wide (posts); what is left, after removing specks under ~0.3 m, is counted per height; a row is a band >= 0.75 m where that count is >= 35% of its peak, dips under ~0.5 m bridged. Guess = rows on the facade with more rows; null = none found. A guess, labelled as one.
